claim: Oct4 (encoded by Pou5f1) and Sox2 are prominent transcription factors (TFs) that regulate early embryonic development.
source: Oct4 (encoded by Pou5f1) and Sox2 are prominent transcription factors (TFs) that regulate early embryonic development.
evidence: This is a general statement about Oct4 and Sox2 that is supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: In mice, Oct4 is expressed in all the cells of the compacted morulae.
source: In mice, Oct4 is expressed in all the cells of the compacted morulae, while Sox2 is first expressed in the inside cell and identified as one of the earliest markers to distinguish the inner from the outer cells (Guo et al., 2010; Palmieri et al., 1994; White et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sox2 is first expressed in the inside cell and identified as one of the earliest markers to distinguish the inner from the outer cells.
source: In mice, Oct4 is expressed in all the cells of the compacted morulae, while Sox2 is first expressed in the inside cell and identified as one of the earliest markers to distinguish the inner from the outer cells (Guo et al., 2010; Palmieri et al., 1994; White et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Both Oct4 and Sox2 are confined to the pluripotent EPI at the late blastocyst stage.
source: Both factors are confined to the pluripotent EPI at the late blastocyst stage (Avilion et al., 2003; Palmieri et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pou5f1 knockout leads to embryonic lethality around embryonic day (E) 4.5.
source: Pou5f1 and Sox2 knockout (KO) leads to embryonic lethality around embryonic day (E) 4.5 and E6.0, respectively (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sox2 knockout leads to embryonic lethality around embryonic day (E) 6.0.
source: Pou5f1 and Sox2 knockout (KO) leads to embryonic lethality around embryonic day (E) 4.5 and E6.0, respectively (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pou5f1-KO or Sox2-KO embryos develop apparently normal EPI.
source: Although Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO embryos develop apparently normal EPI, they fail to give rise to embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998) and Pou5f1-KO embryos cannot contribute to embryonic tissues in chimera assays (Wu et al., 2013), suggesting that Oct4 and Sox2 are required for the EPI to acquire or maintain pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pou5f1-KO or Sox2-KO embryos fail to give rise to embryonic stem cells (ESCs).
source: Although Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO embryos develop apparently normal EPI, they fail to give rise to embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998) and Pou5f1-KO embryos cannot contribute to embryonic tissues in chimera assays (Wu et al., 2013), suggesting that Oct4 and Sox2 are required for the EPI to acquire or maintain pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pou5f1-KO embryos cannot contribute to embryonic tissues in chimera assays.
source: Although Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO embryos develop apparently normal EPI, they fail to give rise to embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998) and Pou5f1-KO embryos cannot contribute to embryonic tissues in chimera assays (Wu et al., 2013), suggesting that Oct4 and Sox2 are required for the EPI to acquire or maintain pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 are required for the EPI to acquire or maintain pluripotency.
source: Although Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO embryos develop apparently normal EPI, they fail to give rise to embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Avilion et al., 2003; Nichols et al., 1998) and Pou5f1-KO embryos cannot contribute to embryonic tissues in chimera assays (Wu et al., 2013), suggesting that Oct4 and Sox2 are required for the EPI to acquire or maintain pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations cited.

claim: Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO mouse embryos still express many pluripotency markers, such as Nanog, Klf4, and Zfp42 (Rex1).
source: Surprisingly, Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO mouse embryos still express many pluripotency markers, such as Nanog, Klf4, and Zfp42 (Rex1) (Avilion et al., 2003; Frum et al., 2013; Le Bin et al., 2014; Stirparo et al., 2021; Wicklow et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The long-lived presence of exogenous Oct4 and Sox2 proteins on DNA was observed in some of the 4-cell blastomeres, that tended toward the ICM rather than the TE.
source: The long-lived presence of exogenous Oct4 and Sox2 proteins on DNA was observed in some of the 4-cell blastomeres, that tended toward the ICM rather than the TE (Plachta et al., 2011; White et al., 2016), suggesting that they may play a role in the initial lineage segregation between ICM and TE.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 may play a role in the initial lineage segregation between ICM and TE.
source: The long-lived presence of exogenous Oct4 and Sox2 proteins on DNA was observed in some of the 4-cell blastomeres, that tended toward the ICM rather than the TE (Plachta et al., 2011; White et al., 2016), suggesting that they may play a role in the initial lineage segregation between ICM and TE.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from cited observations.

claim: Oct4 is thought to contribute to the dramatic gain of chromatin accessibility at the 8-cell stage.
source: Oct4 is also thought to contribute to the dramatic gain of chromatin accessibility at the 8-cell stage (Lu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The loss of OCT4 expression in human embryos compromises blastocyst development, leading to the downregulation of NANOG in the ICM and CDX2 in the TE.
source: Unlike in mouse embryos, the loss of OCT4 expression in human embryos compromises blastocyst development, leading to the downregulation of NANOG in the ICM and CDX2 in the TE (Fogarty et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Oct4 controls zygotic genome activation in zebrafish and human, but not in mice.
source: Oct4 controls zygotic genome activation in zebrafish and human, but not in mice (Gao et al., 2018; Leichsenring et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 play preeminent roles in maintaining the pluripotency-related transcriptional network in ESCs.
source: Oct4 and Sox2 play preeminent roles in maintaining the pluripotency-related transcriptional network in ESCs (Masui et al., 2007; Niwa et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MEK inhibitor (MEKi) promotes the ground state of ESCs by suppressing the PE-inducing ERK signaling pathway.
source: MEK inhibitor (MEKi) promotes the ground state of ESCs by suppressing the PE-inducing ERK signaling pathway (Ying et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In embryos, MEKi has been shown to activate Nanog in ICMs, effectively suppressing the development of PE and directing the entire ICM toward a pluripotent EPI fate.
source: In embryos, MEKi has been shown to activate Nanog in ICMs, effectively suppressing the development of PE and directing the entire ICM toward a pluripotent EPI fate (Nichols et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The naïve pluripotency and readiness for differentiation of MEKi-treated EPI has been confirmed by its contribution to chimaeras with germline transmission.
source: The naïve pluripotency and readiness for differentiation of MEKi-treated EPI has been confirmed by its contribution to chimaeras with germline transmission.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about MEKi-treated EPI.

claim: Four transgenic mouse lines were produced: Pou5f1-KO labeled with mKO2 (Pou5f1mKO2), Sox2-KO labeled with EGFP (Sox2EGFP), floxed Pou5f1 (Pou5f1flox), and floxed Sox2 (Sox2flox).
source: To investigate the role of Oct4 and Sox2 in the development of preimplantation embryos, we produced four transgenic mouse lines: Pou5f1-KO labeled with mKO2 (monomeric kusabira-orange 2, Pou5f1mKO2), Sox2-KO labeled with EGFP (Sox2EGFP), floxed Pou5f1 (Pou5f1flox), and floxed Sox2 (Sox2flox) (Figure 1A and B; Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental design and is supported by the manuscript text and Figure 1A and B.

claim: The expression of mKO2 and EGFP reporters is weak until the 8-cell and blastocyst stages, respectively, when the strong zygotic expression of Oct4 and Sox2 is observed.
source: Although the expression of mKO2 and EGFP is driven by the constitutive mouse PGK promoter, we observed that the expression of these reporters is weak until the 8-cell and blastocyst stages, respectively, when the strong zygotic expression of Oct4 and Sox2 is observed.
evidence: This claim is based on observations made in the study.

claim: Immunostaining results confirmed that the mKO2+ and EGFP+ embryos lost Oct4 and Sox2 proteins, respectively.
source: Immunostaining results confirmed that the mKO2+ and EGFP+ embryos lost Oct4 and Sox2 proteins, respectively (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—source data 2, Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Low-input ATAC-seq and RNA-seq were performed using early (E2.75) and late (E3.25) compacted morulae, as well as early (E3.75) and late (E4.5) ICMs.
source: To assess the genome-wide molecular impact of the loss of Oct4 and Sox2, we performed low-input ATAC-seq and RNA-seq using early (E2.75) and late (E3.25) compacted morulae, as well as early (E3.75) and late (E4.5) ICMs (Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Embryos were pooled based on reporter systems for ATAC-seq because single-embryo samples yielded sparse signals and too few peaks.
source: For ATAC-seq, we pooled embryos based on our reporter systems because single-embryo samples yielded sparse signals and too few peaks (data not shown).
evidence: This claim explains the methodological choice made in the study.

claim: Single morulae or ICMs were collected for RNA-seq to account for embryo-to-embryo variability and detect transcripts with greater sensitivity compared to scRNA-seq.
source: We opted to collect single morulae or ICMs for RNA-seq, as this approach enabled us to account for embryo-to-embryo variability and detect transcripts with greater sensitivity compared to scRNA-seq (Boroviak et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim explains the methodological choice and is supported by a citation.

claim: Embryos were treated with MEKi (PD0325901) from E2.5 to suppress PE development and specify the entire ICM to the EPI.
source: Given that the ICM consists of the progenitors of EPI and PE cells, we treated the embryos with the MEKi (PD0325901) from E2.5 to suppress PE development and specify the entire ICM to the EPI (Nichols et al., 2009; Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental treatment and is supported by a citation and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the ATAC-seq data reveals a clear clustering of samples based on the stages and genotypes.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the ATAC-seq data reveals a clear clustering of samples based on the stages and genotypes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The Pou5f1-KO early and late morulae clustered close to their Ctrl counterparts.
source: The Pou5f1-KO early and late morulae clustered close to their Ctrl counterparts, while the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO early and late ICM samples clustered separately from their Ctrl.
evidence: This claim is based on the PCA analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: The Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO early and late ICM samples clustered separately from their Ctrl.
source: The Pou5f1-KO early and late morulae clustered close to their Ctrl counterparts, while the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO early and late ICM samples clustered separately from their Ctrl.
evidence: This claim is based on the PCA analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: 152,393 peaks were identified across different stages and genotypes in ATAC-seq.
source: In total, 152,393 peaks were identified across different stages and genotypes.
evidence: This claim reports the total number of ATAC-seq peaks identified.

claim: 14,016 (9.2%) peaks showed significant decreases in Pou5f1-KO late ICM.
source: Of these, 14,016 (9.2%) and 6637 (4.4%) showed significant decreases, while 11,884 (7.8%) and 3660 (2.4%) exhibited significant increases in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICM, respectively (Figure 2B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 6,637 (4.4%) peaks showed significant decreases in Sox2-KO late ICM.
source: Of these, 14,016 (9.2%) and 6637 (4.4%) showed significant decreases, while 11,884 (7.8%) and 3660 (2.4%) exhibited significant increases in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICM, respectively (Figure 2B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 11,884 (7.8%) peaks exhibited significant increases in Pou5f1-KO late ICM.
source: Of these, 14,016 (9.2%) and 6637 (4.4%) showed significant decreases, while 11,884 (7.8%) and 3660 (2.4%) exhibited significant increases in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICM, respectively (Figure 2B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 3,660 (2.4%) peaks exhibited significant increases in Sox2-KO late ICM.
source: Of these, 14,016 (9.2%) and 6637 (4.4%) showed significant decreases, while 11,884 (7.8%) and 3660 (2.4%) exhibited significant increases in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICM, respectively (Figure 2B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The number of decreased peaks exceeded that of increased peaks across all the KO samples.
source: The number of decreased peaks exceeded that of increased peaks across all the KO samples.
evidence: This claim is based on the ATAC-seq data analysis.

claim: K-means clustering of the 33,520 differential peaks identifies subsets of open chromatin regions that were differently affected by Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO.
source: K-means clustering of the 33,520 differential peaks identifies subsets of open chromatin regions that were differently affected by Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the clustering analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Peaks highly reliant on both Oct4 and Sox2 show greater enrichment of the OCT-SOX motif compared to peaks more reliant on Oct4 than Sox2.
source: Notably, compared to the peaks more reliant on Oct4 than Sox2 (Figure 2B, clusters 1 and 11), those highly reliant on both Oct4 and Sox2 (clusters 3, 8, and 14) show greater enrichment of the OCT-SOX motif.
evidence: This claim is based on the motif enrichment analysis of clustered peaks.

claim: Peaks more reliant on Oct4 than Sox2 tended to be already open in the morula.
source: The former group tended to be already open in the morula, while the latter group became open in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is based on the temporal analysis of peak accessibility.

claim: Peaks highly reliant on both Oct4 and Sox2 became open in the ICM.
source: The former group tended to be already open in the morula, while the latter group became open in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is based on the temporal analysis of peak accessibility.

claim: Over 96.8% of the significantly changed peaks were identified as putative enhancers located distally to the transcription start sites (TSSs).
source: Over 96.8% of the significantly changed peaks were identified as putative enhancers located distally to the transcription start sites (TSSs) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the genomic location analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The decreased ATAC-seq peaks were enriched with Sox2 CUT&RUN signals.
source: Remarkably, the decreased ATAC-seq peaks were enriched with Sox2 CUT&RUN signals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparison with Sox2 CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The peaks decreasing in the Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO late ICMs were frequently bound by Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog, and enriched with the active enhancer mark H3K27ac in ESCs.
source: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data in ESCs (Marson et al., 2008; Whyte et al., 2012) shows that the peaks decreasing in the Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO late ICMs were frequently bound by Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog, and enriched with the active enhancer mark H3K27ac (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Maternal KO embryos clustered together with wildtype embryos in the PCA of RNA-seq data.
source: Maternal KO embryos (circles in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) clustered together with wildtype embryos (triangles and squares) in the PCA, consistent with previous studies reporting no observable phenotype in maternal KO embryos (Avilion et al., 2003; Frum et al., 2013; Kehler et al., 2004; Nichols et al., 1998; Wicklow et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA analysis and citations to previous studies.

claim: In morulae, Pou5f1-KO had only a minor effect on the transcriptome.
source: In morulae, Pou5f1-KO had only a minor effect on the transcriptome (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A progressively profound impact of Pou5f1-KO on the transcriptome was observed from the morula to the late ICM.
source: We observed a progressively profound impact of Pou5f1-KO on the transcriptome from the morula to the late ICM, mirroring patterns at the chromatin level (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: The transcriptome in Sox2-KO morulae was not significantly affected.
source: As Sox2 is only expressed at very low levels until the blastocyst stage anyway, the transcriptome in Sox2-KO morulae was not significantly affected.
evidence: This claim is based on the RNA-seq data and the known expression pattern of Sox2.

claim: Pou5f1-KO altered the expression of 2,485 (15.8%) genes in the late ICM.
source: Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO altered the expression of 2485 (15.8%) and 967 (6.1%) genes in the late ICM, respectively (Figure 2D; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Sox2-KO altered the expression of 967 (6.1%) genes in the late ICM.
source: Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO altered the expression of 2485 (15.8%) and 967 (6.1%) genes in the late ICM, respectively (Figure 2D; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Pou5f1-KO had a greater effect than Sox2-KO on both the chromatin accessibility and the transcriptome.
source: Pou5f1-KO had a greater effect than Sox2-KO on both the chromatin accessibility and the transcriptome (Figure 2A–D), suggesting Oct4 may play a more important role than Sox2.
evidence: This claim is based on the comparison of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Oct4 may play a more important role than Sox2.
source: Pou5f1-KO had a greater effect than Sox2-KO on both the chromatin accessibility and the transcriptome (Figure 2A–D), suggesting Oct4 may play a more important role than Sox2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparative analysis of KO effects.

claim: The earlier developmental arrest of Pou5f1-KO embryos at E4.5 compared to Sox2-KO embryos at E6.0 is consistent with Oct4 playing a more important role than Sox2.
source: This is consistent with the earlier developmental arrest of Pou5f1-KO embryos at E4.5 compared to Sox2-KO embryos at E6.0.
evidence: This claim is based on the observed developmental phenotypes.

claim: Down- and upregulated genes identified in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs show enrichment with genes exhibiting down- and upregulation, respectively, in studies without MEKi.
source: Down- and upregulated genes identified in our Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs show enrichment with genes exhibiting down- and upregulation, respectively, in the studies without MEKi (Li et al., 2023; Stirparo et al., 2021; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–D), confirming that MEKi did not alter the molecular functions of Oct4 and Sox2 in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis comparing with published data.

claim: MEKi did not alter the molecular functions of Oct4 and Sox2 in the ICM.
source: Down- and upregulated genes identified in our Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs show enrichment with genes exhibiting down- and upregulation, respectively, in the studies without MEKi (Li et al., 2023; Stirparo et al., 2021; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–D), confirming that MEKi did not alter the molecular functions of Oct4 and Sox2 in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison with studies without MEKi.

claim: Genes close to the decreased peak centers were frequently downregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) shows that the genes close to the decreased peak centers were frequently downregulated, whereas those near the increased peak centers were upregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos (Figure 2E; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Genes near the increased peak centers were upregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) shows that the genes close to the decreased peak centers were frequently downregulated, whereas those near the increased peak centers were upregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos (Figure 2E; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The expression of Utf1 and the accessibility of its well-characterized OCT-SOX enhancer decreased in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs.
source: For example, the expression of Utf1, a known target of Oct4 and Sox2, as well as the accessibility of its well-characterized OCT-SOX enhancer decreased in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs (Nishimoto et al., 1999; Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2F and G and a citation.

claim: The expression of Fgfr2 and the accessibility of ATAC-seq peaks within its introns increased in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM.
source: On the other hand, the expression of Fgfr2 and the accessibility of ATAC-seq peaks within its introns increased in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM.
evidence: This claim is based on the ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Sap30 and Uhrf1 are previously unknown targets of Oct4 and Sox2.
source: In addition, integration of the ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data allowed us to infer previously unknown targets of Oct4 and Sox2, such as Sap30 and Uhrf1, which are essential for somatic cell reprogramming and embryonic development (Figure 2F and G; Cao et al., 2019; Li et al., 2017; Maenohara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the integration of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Sap30 and Uhrf1 are essential for somatic cell reprogramming and embryonic development.
source: In addition, integration of the ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data allowed us to infer previously unknown targets of Oct4 and Sox2, such as Sap30 and Uhrf1, which are essential for somatic cell reprogramming and embryonic development (Figure 2F and G; Cao et al., 2019; Li et al., 2017; Maenohara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 play a crucial role in shaping the chromatin landscape and transcriptome in the ICM.
source: Taken together, the data presented so far indicate that Oct4 and Sox2 play a crucial role in shaping the chromatin landscape and transcriptome in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is a summary conclusion based on the presented data.

claim: Apparently normal development of the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos was observed up to the blastocyst stage.
source: Consequently, we observed apparently normal development of the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO embryos up to the blastocyst stage.
evidence: This claim is based on the morphological observations of the embryos.

claim: Many of the differential ATAC-seq peaks were consistently changed in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICMs.
source: As expected, many of the differential ATAC-seq peaks were consistently changed in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO late ICMs (Figure 3A, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the scatter plot analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There are a number of peaks exclusively changed in either Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO ICMs.
source: However, there are a number of peaks exclusively changed in either Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO ICMs.
evidence: This claim is based on the ATAC-seq data analysis.

claim: The genes around the consistently decreased peaks were enriched for terms related to pluripotency and preimplantation embryonic development.
source: The genes around the consistently decreased peaks were enriched for terms related to pluripotency and preimplantation embryonic development, such as cellular response to LIF signaling and stem cell population maintenance (Figure 3B, upper panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by the GREAT ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The consistently elevated peaks preferentially located near the genes related to extraembryonic lineages and organogenesis.
source: The consistently elevated peaks preferentially located near the genes related to extraembryonic lineages and organogenesis, such as embryonic placenta, extraembryonic trophoblast, muscle, and neural tube (Figure 3B, lower panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by the GREAT ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The genes near the peaks which decreased only in the Pou5f1-KO but not in the Sox2-KO ICM were enriched with terms of LIF signaling and blastocyst formation.
source: Interestingly, the genes near the peaks which decreased only in the Pou5f1-KO but not in the Sox2-KO ICM were enriched with terms of LIF signaling and blastocyst formation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Many known pluripotency genes, such as Klf2, Etv5, Prdm14, and Pecam1, were downregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM.
source: At the transcriptional level, many known pluripotency genes, such as Klf2, Etv5, Prdm14, and Pecam1, were downregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Gata3, Cdx2, and Eomes, which are important for TE development and differentiation, were upregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM.
source: In contrast, Gata3, Cdx2, and Eomes, which are important for TE development and differentiation (Ralston et al., 2010; Russ et al., 2000; Strumpf et al., 2005), were upregulated in the Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICM.
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data and citations to previous studies.

claim: Nanog, Esrrb, and Klf4 were significantly downregulated in the Pou5f1-KO ICM.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Nanog, Esrrb, and Klf4 were significantly downregulated in the Pou5f1-KO ICM, whereas they were not or only slightly downregulated in the Sox2-KO ICM (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Nanog, Esrrb, and Klf4 were not or only slightly downregulated in the Sox2-KO ICM.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Nanog, Esrrb, and Klf4 were significantly downregulated in the Pou5f1-KO ICM, whereas they were not or only slightly downregulated in the Sox2-KO ICM (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Downregulation of Pecam1 was confirmed at the protein level.
source: Downregulation of Pecam1 was confirmed at the protein level (Figure 3E, Figure 3—source data 1, Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Chromatin accessibility at putative enhancers of Pecam1 decreased in Pou5f1- and Sox2-KO ICMs.
source: Chromatin accessibility at its putative enhancers also decreased accordingly (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 activated the components of several epigenetic modifiers, such as Ezh2 and Sap30.
source: Oct4 and Sox2 activated the components of several epigenetic modifiers, such as Ezh2 (PRC2 H3K27me2/3 methyltransferase) and Sap30 (a component of mSin3A histone deacetylase complex) (Figure 2F and G; Supplementary file 5), suggesting their potential contribution to establishing the ICM-specific epigenetic status through regulation of the epigenetic modifiers.
evidence: This claim is supported by the RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 potentially contribute to establishing the ICM-specific epigenetic status through regulation of the epigenetic modifiers.
source: Oct4 and Sox2 activated the components of several epigenetic modifiers, such as Ezh2 (PRC2 H3K27me2/3 methyltransferase) and Sap30 (a component of mSin3A histone deacetylase complex) (Figure 2F and G; Supplementary file 5), suggesting their potential contribution to establishing the ICM-specific epigenetic status through regulation of the epigenetic modifiers.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the activation of epigenetic modifiers.

claim: Oct4 and Sox2 regulate a large number of TFs, epigenetic factors, and signaling pathways in the ICM.
source: Taken together, the above data show that Oct4 and Sox2 regulate a large number of TFs, epigenetic factors, and signaling pathways in the ICM.
evidence: This claim is a summary conclusion based on the presented data.

claim: The OCT-SOX, OCT, and SOX motifs were among the most enriched motifs in the group of decreased peaks in Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO ICMs.
source: As expected, the OCT-SOX, OCT, and SOX motifs were also among the most enriched motifs in the group of decreased peaks in Pou5f1- or Sox2-KO ICMs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The expression of core pluripotency TFs in the morula does not seem sufficient to induce the mature pluripotent state at this stage.
